mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% signals tighter monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4% indicates a tightening labor market, which may lead to wage inflation and reduced corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive when UNRATE < 4%, or the mechanism fails to predict negative returns in >30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals improved consumer confidence and increased demand for goods and services, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in >40% of cases when HOUST increases by >5%, or Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests increased economic activity and productivity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in >35% of cases when INDPRO increases by >1%, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) and high federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) creates a scenario where inflationary pressures and borrowing costs squeeze corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive in >40% of cases when CPIAUCSL > 250 and FEDFUNDS > 2%, or Rank IC < 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates reduced consumer spending, which may lead to decreased corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in >35% of cases when RSAFS declines by >2%, or Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) combined with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to wage inflation and reduced corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive in >30% of cases when PAYEMS increases by >200k and UNRATE < 4%, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which may lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in >40% of cases when GDPC1 increases by >2%, or Rank IC < 0.04.
